lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Elizabeth's early assurance that she already understands Robert's words.

lines.text: While I am writing, comes in Arabel with such a face.
lines.note: The first family storm breaking around their secret engagement.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert's intimate confession about shortening visits to take Elizabeth's hand.

lines.text: I have just come from the vestry of Paddington chapel, and bore it very well, and saw nobody except one woman.
lines.note: Elizabeth's first successful return to chapel after her nervousness.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The sudden loss of Flush, one of their shared private concerns.

lines.text: I am rejoiced that poor Flush is found again, dearest—altogether rejoiced.
lines.note: Robert's rejoicing at Flush's recovery, answering Elizabeth's alarm.

lines.text: Dearest, you are a prophet, I suppose—there can be no denying it.
lines.note: Elizabeth recognises Robert as a prophet as the household removal forces their decision.

lines.text: I look back, and in every one point, every word and gesture, every letter, every silence—you have been entirely perfect to me—I would not change one word, one look.
lines.note: Robert looks back and declares he would not change one word or look.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth's exhausted but relieved report on the wedding day.

lines.text: All that I am, I owe you—if I enjoy anything now and henceforth, it is through you.
lines.note: Elizabeth's gratitude for Robert having lifted her into life.

lines.text: I did hate so, to have to take off the ring!
lines.note: Elizabeth's pain at having to remove the wedding ring.

lines.text: You take my words from me—I ‘exult’ in the irrevocability of this precious bestowal of yourself on me—come what will my life has borne flower and fruit—it is a glorious, successful, felicitous life, I thank God and you.
lines.note: Robert exults in the irrevocability of Elizabeth's gift of herself.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Elizabeth's farewell-eve certainty that she will have only Robert.

lines.text: I begin to think that none are so bold as the timid, when they are fairly roused.
lines.note: Elizabeth's final reflection on Wilson's unexpected boldness.
